doc.title: Ralph Humphrey interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003

title: Hopes for the new music, jazz needing to change, and goodbye
summary: Humphrey hopes the Greek project stands out, argues music should be of its time and jazz may need to change; the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well it’s been a fascinating conversation and it’s been a pleasure to meet you.
Thank you for talking with me.
And I wish you the best of luck with the Greek music. You know you said it’s different than anything that’s out there and maybe that’s what’ll get it out there.

Yeah, we’re kind of hoping that, yeah. Because it’s nice to hear something different come out. Because I think a lot of the traditional jazz stuff continues to be what I would call regurgitated in new groups and new artists and whatnot and it’s all great but I don’t know if the effort is to try to improve what’s already been done, but I know that music — and I said it in my clinics also — is that music needs to be of its time, and for the people of its time. And so if jazz needs to change to do that then I think jazz needs to change. Let the tradition be the tradition but then let it allow to be grown and to go somewhere else, and maybe not call it jazz anymore, but I don’t know what to call these new things that I hear.
All right. Well on that note, thanks a lot.
